items.prompt: White has just taken the pawn on d4 with the queen. Black to move. One pawn move attacks the queen and begins to shut in the bishop on b3. Find it.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the pawn move to c5 is the engine's best.
After the move the pawn on c5 attacks the queen on d4.
After 8...c5 the engine rates the position at least 2.5 pawns in Black's favour (depth 16).

hints: Which Black pawn can attack the queen on d4 in one move?
The pawn will later go on to c4. What will it attack there?
The move is c7 to c5.
items.explain: The pawn on c5 attacks the queen, so White must spend a move on it. Next the pawn can go to c4 and attack the bishop on b3, whose exits are covered. A developing move such as the knight to f6 lets the queen settle, and the engine rates it about level. At depth 16 the pawn move leaves Black more than 2.5 pawns ahead.

feedback_by_move.g8f6: A sound developing move, but it lets the queen settle: the engine rates it about level, so the trap is not used.
feedback_by_move.c8b7: Sound, but quiet. It does not attack the queen, so the bishop on b3 is never put under pressure.

items.prompt: White to move. Tap every square the bishop on b3 can move to.

claims.statement: The bishop can go to a4 or c4 and nowhere else.
The pawn on b5 attacks a4.
The pawn on b5 also attacks c4.

hints: Look at the squares next to the bishop. Which of them hold White pawns?
Two diagonals are blocked by White's own pawns on a2 and c2.
Only a4 and c4 are free.
items.explain: The pawns on a2 and c2 block two diagonals, so the bishop has only a4 and c4. The pawn on b5 attacks both, and the pawn on c4 attacks the bishop itself. One pawn guards both exits.

items.prompt: Same cage, one change: White's pawn stands on a3, not a2. White to move. Tap every square the bishop on b3 can move to.

claims.statement: The bishop can go to a2, a4 or c4.
No Black piece attacks a2.
At depth 16 the position is within 1.2 pawns of level.

hints: Compare with the first cage. Which square has opened?
The a2 square used to hold a White pawn.
a2, a4 and c4.
items.explain: With the pawn on a3 the corner square a2 is free, and nothing of Black's attacks it, so the bishop has a safe retreat. The cage has a hole: with Ba2 White loses only about half a pawn, against about four pawns when the pawn stands on a2.

items.prompt: White to move. The pawn on d4 can be taken, but the engine prefers three other moves. Find one of them.

claims.statement: At depth 16 a4, c3 and Bd5 are all within 0.4 pawns of the engine's best.
At depth 16 the queen capture is at least 2.5 pawns worse than the best move.

hints: Before you take, count the bishop's exits after Black's pawn reaches c4.
A pawn move that gives the bishop a flight square or hits b5 changes the count.
a4, c3 or Bd5.
items.explain: The pawn move a4 attacks the pawn on b5, c3 asks the pawn on d4 a question and the bishop to d5 steps out of the net. Each keeps the bishop from being shut in. The queen grab loses the bishop for two pawns: at depth 16 it is at least 2.5 pawns worse than the best move.

feedback_by_move.d1d4: The grab walks into ...c5 and ...c4: the bishop on b3 has only a4 and c4, and the pawn on b5 covers both.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's knight on e7 stands in front of the queen on d8, and White's bishop on g5 aims through the knight. Find the move that adds a second attacker to e7.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the knight move to d5 is the engine's best.
After the move two White pieces attack e7.

hints: Which White piece can reach a square that attacks e7?
The knight on c3 has a jump that attacks e7 and also the pawn on c7.
Knight c3 to d5.
items.explain: The knight on d5 and the bishop on g5 both attack e7, and the knight on e7 is the only thing between the bishop and the queen. If that knight ever moves, the bishop takes the queen. The engine agrees: at depth 16 the knight move is its first choice.

items.prompt: Black to move. The knight on d5 attacks the knight on e7 and the pawn on c7. Does 10...Nxd5 lose material for Black?

claims.statement: At depth 16 capturing on d5 is at least four pawns worse than the best move.
Three Black pieces defend e7 (queen, king and bishop).
After the knight leaves e7 the bishop on g5 attacks the queen on d8.

hints: After the black knight takes on d5, which line does the bishop on g5 see?
Look at the diagonal from g5 through e7.
Yes: the bishop takes the queen.
items.explain: When the knight leaves e7 the bishop on g5 sees the queen on d8 and takes it. The knight is not pinned to the king, so the move is legal, but it costs the queen for a knight and a bishop at best. At depth 16 it is at least four pawns worse than the engine's best move.

items.prompt: Same position, one change: Black's queen stands on d7, not d8. Black to move. Does 10...Nxd5 lose material for Black?

claims.statement: After 10...Nxd5 the engine rates the position within 1.5 pawns of level (depth 16).
The bishop on g5 does not attack the queen on d7.

hints: Which square does the bishop on g5 attack through e7?
The queen is no longer on that diagonal.
No, the tie is gone.
items.explain: The queen has left the long diagonal, so the knight on e7 is free to move: the bishop attacks d8, but nothing stands there. The capture on d5 trades knights and the engine rates the position about level.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has played 10...f6 and the pawn attacks the bishop on g5. Find the move that wins material or the initiative.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the bishop capture on f6 is the engine's best.
After the capture only the pawn on g7 can recapture on f6.
After the capture the bishop on f6 attacks the pawn on g7.
At depth 16 White stands at least 1.2 pawns better here.

hints: The bishop is attacked. Is retreating the only way to save it?
A bishop on f6 would attack two Black units next to the king. Which?
Bishop g5 takes f6.
items.explain: The bishop takes f6 and now attacks the knight on e7 and the pawn on g7. If the g-pawn recaptures, the knight on d5 jumps to f6 with check, as in the game. The engine prefers the capture to the knight jump by more than a pawn.

feedback_by_move.d5f6: The knight jump is check, but after ...gxf6 the bishop is attacked as well: the engine rates it clearly below the bishop capture.
feedback_by_move.g5h4: A retreat keeps the bishop but gives the initiative back; the engine rates the capture more than a pawn higher.

items.prompt: Black to move. In the game Black played 10...f6, which costs more than a pawn. Find one of two moves the engine rates better.

claims.statement: At depth 16 Nxb3 and c5 are within 0.2 pawns of each other and the best moves.

hints: The bishop on b3 is the piece White spent time on. Can it be traded?
A pawn move can attack the queen on d4.
Nxb3 or c5.
items.explain: The knight on a5 can take the bishop on b3, or the pawn can go to c5 and attack the queen. Both leave the pawn cover of the king alone. The engine rates both more than a pawn better than 10...f6.

feedback_by_move.f7f6: The pawn move attacks the bishop but loosens the squares around the king: the engine rates it about a pawn worse than the two better moves.
feedback_by_move.e7d5: Taking on d5 hands White the queen for a bishop.
